rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about or consider criminal history until after a conditional offer, and may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer, only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods may be considered, with an individualized assessment and written reasons if the offer is withdrawn.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer; look-back 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd), 1 yr (4th)
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer
rules.effective_date_note: Approved June 18, 2021; effective first day of the seventh month next following enactment = 2022-01-01 (computed).
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.penalty: Up to $1,000 / $5,000 / $10,000 depending on prior violations; enforced by Division on Civil Rights; no private court action; application fee may be ordered returned.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income (incl. Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone because of the lawful source of their income or rent payment, such as a Section 8 voucher. Complaints go to the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days or Superior Court within two years.
rules.key_value: ban on source-of-income (incl. Section 8 voucher) discrimination
rules.quoted_span: This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income
rules.effective_date_note: Documents do not state when source-of-income protection took effect.
rules.exemptions: Rental of one apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious-organization preference.
rules.penalty: Up to $10,000 for a first offense.

unverifiable_exemptions: one apartment in owner-occupied two-family dwelling

rules.title: Residential rental application fee cap ($50, CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent cannot charge more than $50 for an application or similar fee to lease a residential rental. The cap is CPI-adjusted annually; the wrongly charged amount is remitted to the applicant from penalties.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
rules.effective_date_note: Approved 2026-01-20; effective first day of fourth month next following = 2026-05-01 (computed).
rules.exemptions: Units in one- or two-family dwellings; NJ Real Estate Commission licensees unless landlord.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first, $750 second, $1,000 each subsequent offense.

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law (cap, trust/interest, return)
rules.requirement: Security deposit may not exceed 1.5 months' rent (prepaid last month's rent counts), with yearly increases capped at 10%; first month's rent may also be collected. Deposits are held in trust in an interest-bearing NJ account with interest to the tenant, and must be returned with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days of tenancy end, with double damages if wrongfully withheld.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent max; return within 30 days
rules.quoted_span: one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less
rules.effective_date_note: Documents do not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (tenant can opt in); seasonal rentals exempt from interest-account section.
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongly withheld plus costs and fees; tenant may apply deposit plus 7% interest to rent if notice/interest not provided.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in)

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act (good cause, notices to quit, relocation, penalties)
rules.requirement: A landlord may remove a tenant only through court process and needs a statutory good cause (nonpayment, disorderly conduct, lease breach, owner occupancy, conversion, etc.); lease non-renewal also requires good cause. Except for nonpayment, a written Notice to Quit (3 days to 3 years depending on ground) is required; lockouts are illegal, and misuse of occupancy/removal notices carries treble damages.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; Notice to Quit 3 days to 3 years
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.effective_date_note: Session law P.L.1974, c.49 cited in D065; only the year is available.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-/three-family dwellings are governed by the more limited N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2; hotel/motel transient or seasonal guests; unit held in trust for developmentally disabled relative.
rules.penalty: Treble damages plus fees; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation for misuse of removal notices.

unverifiable_exemptions: unit held in trust for developmentally disabled family member

rules.title: NJ tenant reprisal protection
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict, substantially change lease terms, or refuse to renew in retaliation for a tenant exercising protected rights such as enforcing lease/legal rights, good-faith health or safety complaints, or joining a tenant organization.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10).
rules.effective_date_note: Documents do not state an effective date.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's algorithmic rent-pricing software that pools nonpublic competitor data or facilitates parallel pricing, and no one may perform such a coordinating function. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act, and municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic coordinators / parallel pricing coordination in residential rentals
rules.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
rules.effective_date_note: Approved 2026-07-20; effective first day of the twelfth month next following enactment = 2027-07-01 (computed); D060 also states July 1, 2027.
rules.exemptions: Research/statistical use, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage databases, government affordability controls; inpatient medical, long-term care and detention facilities.
rules.penalty: Violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act (sections 6-17 enforcement apply); AG complaint portal.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) bars municipal ordinances that conflict with the act.
rules.conflict_note: May preempt conflicting local ordinances (Jersey City § 218-12, Hoboken ch. 158, Art. II) from 2027-07-01; flag for human review.

unverifiable_exemptions: inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, detention facilities

no_rule_findings.finding: New Jersey has no statewide rent control or cap on rent increases; municipalities may adopt rent control or leveling. Increases need proper notice and must not be unconscionable. Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5).
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.

dropped_candidates.reason: New-construction exemption from local rent control is not a rule of its own; belongs in coverage of local rent control rules (30 years, construction completed).
Represented as no_rule_finding for state rent_increase_limits.
Foreclosure Fairness Act mentioned in passing in a broad handbook; not the principal just-cause law.
Condo/co-op conversion protected tenancy is a niche statute mentioned in passing in a broad handbook; not the principal law.
